headline: No planner configuration clears both gates: high reasoning is what lifts every task to the pass rate, and it is also what breaks the latency budget.
lede: Brisk-S high+retry (L) holds the pass rate in every task at {cost_per_month.brisk-s.high.r1} a month, but its p95 over all cases is {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.high.r1.p95} against a {criteria.p95.threshold} budget. A fix that lifts Brisk-S low+retry (J) on multi-hop and ambiguous queries, or a declaration of which gate gives, would settle the call.

caveats.label: Latency measured only across all cases
caveats.material_if: Material only if the four tasks do not split the cases between them; if they do, an overall p95 over budget means at least one task is over it too, so no high-reasoning configuration can pass the latency gate as declared.

caveats.label: Per-task case counts unstated
caveats.material_if: Material to which near miss is closest, not to whether anything passes: per-task rates carry no count, so every gate is read on its point estimate and the noise on thin gaps is sized only under counts assumed from traffic shares.

caveats.label: Best of many configurations
caveats.material_if: Material if a re-run reads the two high-reasoning configurations' thin per-task clearances lower, as the best of {n_candidates} tends to; that would leave fewer options on the pass-rate side, not more.
Material only to the comparisons between configurations, which are read unpaired and so err wide; the gate readings are absolute and do not rest on it.

decision.text: The two gates pull opposite ways along one setting. High reasoning brings Brisk-S and Atlas-M to the pass rate in every task and pushes their p95 past the budget; low or no reasoning keeps Brisk-S inside the budget overall and leaves it short on multi-hop and ambiguous queries.

Atlas-M high+retry (F) is out on every axis but pass rate, and there it is not separated from Brisk-S high+retry (L) while costing {cost.gap.atlas-m.high.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.multiple} as much. Every Nano-XS configuration misses the pass rate in every task.

L clears multi-hop by {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.multihop.gap} points; at an assumed {assumed.share.spread.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.task.multihop.n} multi-hop cases a fresh run would read it below the line {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.task.multihop.wrong_side} of the time. J's date-math rate sits exactly on the line.
Either a Brisk-S low+retry (J) that clears multi-hop and ambiguous queries, or the planner's owner declaring whether the latency budget or the pass rate gives. Neither was declared in advance.

claims.text: Only {count.passing.pass_rate} of the {n_candidates} configurations hold the pass rate in every task, and both run past the latency budget across all cases.

evidence.caption: Pass rate by task for the two configurations that hold the gate everywhere and the fastest near miss, against the {criteria.pass_rate.threshold} gate.
Latency from p50 to p95 across all cases against the {criteria.p95.threshold} budget; no task's own p95 was recorded.

claims.text: On Brisk-S with a retry, high reasoning adds {lever.reasoning.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.effect} points of pass rate over low, not separated from zero, while it moves p95 from {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.low.r1.p95} to {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.high.r1.p95}.

evidence.caption: What each Brisk-S setting buys in pass rate, in points with unpaired intervals; a retry helps at every reasoning level.

claims.text: Atlas-M high+retry (F) buys no separated pass rate over Brisk-S high+retry (L) and costs {cost.gap.atlas-m.high.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.multiple} as much.

evidence.caption: Atlas-M minus Brisk-S on pass rate; per-task rows carry no interval because no task states its count.

claims.text: Brisk-S low+retry (J) runs inside the budget across all cases, with L costing {cost.gap.brisk-s.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.multiple} as much, and misses the pass rate only on multi-hop and ambiguous queries, where its kept failures are planning errors.

evidence.caption: One kept failure per task for J: a collapsed two-hop query, an off-by-one date window, and a guess where a clarifying question was expected.

explore.binds: Whether the high-reasoning configurations can pass the latency gate
explore.outcome: No budget changes today's reading, because no task's p95 was recorded. If the tasks split the cases, L would need a budget no lower than its overall p95 of {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.high.r1.p95}.

explore.binds: Whether the fast Brisk-S configurations can pass
explore.outcome: J's weakest task reads {task.multihop.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.mean}; a gate at or below that would admit it on pass rate, its per-task latency still unknown.

omitted.why: Each misses the pass rate in every task by a wide gap; cheapest by far, but no setting brings it near the gate.

omitted.what: Atlas-M with reasoning off or low, and the no-retry high-reasoning arms
omitted.why: Each misses the pass rate on multi-hop; none changes the reading.

omitted.what: Calls per task, extra calls and outcome shares
omitted.why: Describe how plans fail; no gate reads them and they do not change the call.

omitted.what: Retry helps Nano-XS more than Atlas-M
omitted.why: A real interaction, but on a model that is out on every task.
The gate reads the p95; the p50 is shown only as the start of each latency bar.

next.text: Re-record latency per task for the Brisk-S configurations, from the same runs if per-trial timings were kept.
next.settles: Reads the latency gate where it was declared, and shows whether L misses on every task or only on the slow ones, which would make routing those tasks an option worth running.

next.text: Fix multi-hop decomposition and ambiguous-entity clarification in J's planner, then re-run it on larger multi-hop and ambiguous sets; at an assumed {assumed.share.spread.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.task.multihop.n} multi-hop cases today, about {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.task.multihop.cases_needed_two_sided} would confirm today's miss with a two-sided interval.
next.settles: Whether a configuration inside the budget can clear the pass rate in every task.

next.text: The planner's owner declares which gate gives if no fix closes the gap: the latency budget or the per-task pass rate.
next.settles: Turns the choice between L and J into a decision.

method.text: Each of the {n_candidates} configurations ran the same {scoreboard.brisk-s.high.r1.cases} queries once, none lost, across four tasks with traffic shares; the snapshot states no per-task case count.
A query passes or fails; the campaign states no further definition, and kept failures are graded against an expected tool-call plan.

Pass rate at least {criteria.pass_rate.threshold} and p95 latency at most {criteria.p95.threshold}, each in every task; both read on the point estimate. Only overall p95 was recorded, so the latency gate is unknown in every task, never failed.

Binomial intervals at the {lever.reasoning.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.level} level, computed from each configuration's cases and combined as independent for differences, which reads wide where configurations ran the same cases; no correction across the many comparisons.
Sized under an assumed count, each task's share of traffic times the configuration's cases, and labelled as such.
No production configuration was declared, so every comparison is between two candidates' own figures.
Cost per 1,000 planner calls, and per month at the declared volume of {meta.volume_per_month} calls.
